newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end sharply up on rebound.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end sharply up on rebound.

text.p: China stock indices ended up sharply on a strong technical rebound, but the market mood remained cautious with volumes low and investors still fearing official intervention to force prices down further, brokers said.

The Shanghai B index went up 3.625 points to 85.763 points while the Shanghai A index rose 30.829 points, or 2.36 percent, to 1,338.650. The SSE30 blue chip index put on 60.167 points, or 1.54 percent, to 3,968.505.
The Shenzhen B share index, meanwhile, gained 4.73 points, or 3.23 percent, to 151.07 and its domestic currency A share index soared 16.24 points, or 3.83 percent, to 440.48.

Institutions, encouraged by a rise in the A share index, were seen supporting Shanghai B shares, brokers said. Investors were encouraged by a lack of further official crackdown measures in recent days, they added.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development and Shanghai Dazhong Taxi got strong support from institutions, triggering some bargain-hunting buying, brokers said.
Shanghai Lujiazui traded actively, ending up $0.068, or 4.99 percent, to $1.430 on volume of 1.6 million shares.
Shanghai Dazhong was the second-biggest winner on institutional buying, soaring $0.140, or 9.21 percent, to $1.660 on volume of 545,000 shares.

"Institutions made use of a strong rebound in the (Shanghai) A shares to boost B shares," one broker said. "But trading volume did not grow, indicating the market is likely to consolidate in the next few days."
"The Shenzhen B index's rally was purely technical, and I expect it to correct in a narrow band in the near future," said Peter Ho, an analyst at PBI Securities HK Ltd.

On Monday, the B index closed down 4.47 percent after a leading A share firm, the Shenzhen Development Bank, postponed a shareholders' meeting due to a probe into share trading irregularities, analysts said.
On Tuesday, the Shenzhen bank traded at 37.08 yuan, down 0.72 yuan, or 1.9 percent, making it the biggest loser in the Shenzhen A share market.
"People are nervous about any rebound, thinking it will spur the authorities to crack down on the markets," an analyst at China Southern Securities said.
The government began to implement policies to rein in stock speculation at the start of May, by which time the A and B indices had surged more than 50 percent from the start of 1997.
Diesel concern Changchai Co Ltd was the sharpest gainer in the Shenzhen B share market, up HK$0.64, or 9.61 percent, to HK$7.30.
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor was the star on the Shanghai B share market, soaring $0.072 or 10.02 percent to $0.790 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded on institutional cross trading, ending up $0.028, or 3.99 percent, at $0.728 on volume of 2.8 million shares.
